newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn turns up late on weather jitters, charts.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn turns up late on weather jitters, charts.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher as the market quietly firmed late amid weather jitters and technical buy signals including short covering, traders said.

"The market is heavily short. We see the charts trying to put in a bottom on corn and it is poised technically for a nice rally," said Dan Cekander, analyst for FIMAT Futures. "But obviously we could go a dime either way on weather, it's up to the weather guys."

The market struggled between a neutral USDA supply/demand forecast, persistent nearly ideal crop weather and some private outlooks at midday that cast uncertainty about whether the good crop weather would continue through the weekend.

"On the whole I was not surprised at all by any of the numbers (USDA) and the next few weeks will determine where we go," said John Zanutto, vice president for Merrill Lynch Futures. "Next week's rain event or non-rain event will do more to flat prices than any of these numbers."
USDA Friday pegged 1996-97 (Sep-Aug) U.S. corn carryover at 916 million bushels, above the June forecast for 909 million but within trade expectations.
Corn closed two to 4-1/4 cents higher, with July up 3-3/4 cents at $2.51-1/2 a bushel. Dec was up 2-1/2 at $2.37.
The 1997-98 U.S. corn carryover was estimated by USDA to total 1.196 billion bushels, above the June government forecast for 909 million bushels.

While the government's supply/demand report generated substantial discussion, the entry this month of the U.S. corn crop into its key pollination stage of development kept Midwest weather on the front burner, traders noted.

This week saw periodic release of outlooks for drier and hotter weather in the Midwest by the weekend which could interfere with crop development. But sources said the jury is out on the weather impact on corn futures until the resumption of CBOT corn futures trading overnight Sunday and again during Monday's regular day trading session.

"We have actually a little more rain (forecast) in eastern Kansas, Missouri and southern Iowa, increasing the amounts there but other than that, there was no change," FIMAT's Cekander said. "I get the impression we'll be up harder (Sunday night and Monday) if there's no rain than down if there is rain."
Cargill Inc bought two million bushels of December, Smith Barney bought two million bushels of December as did SAK Futures, traders said.
Prudential Securities sold 3.5 million bushels of December and Dean Witter sold four million bushels of December, traders said.

In spread trading, Tenco Inc did one million bushels of July/Decmeber at 13-1/2 cents, premium July, Term Commodities spread one million December/July at 13-1/2 cents, premium July and Refco Inc did one million September/July at 13-1/2 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 60,000 contracts, above the 41,623 traded Thursday.

In corn options, Lind Waldock bought 1,000 December $2.50 puts and sold 1,000 December $2.30 puts at 13-1/4 cents, Farmers Commodities bought 800 September $2.50 calls at three to 3-1/4 cents and USA Trading bought 84 December $4.40 puts and sold 1,200 December $2.00 puts, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 19,000 contracts, slightly below the 19,724 traded Thursday.
